Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberShield Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberShield's results for the second quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Security Officer; and Casey Wong, VP of Sales.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberShield continues to demonstrate leadership in the cybersecurity market. We achieved record bookings in the second quarter, driven by strong demand for our integrated security platform, ShieldXDR, and our expanding global presence. The positive customer feedback about ShieldXDR and the resulting acceleration in platform adoption is very encouraging.

We are focused on six strategic priorities: staying ahead of the evolving threat landscape, maintaining low churn rates while addressing key drivers, advancing progress on our core strategic initiatives, providing a clear full-year revenue and profitability outlook, accelerating the acquisition of new customers, and growing the number of customers with ARR over $100,000.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. We delivered another quarter of strong financial results. Total revenue for the second quarter was $320 million, representing a 42% increase year-over-year. We saw significant growth in our subscription revenue, which now accounts for 85% of our total revenue. Gross margin was 88%, while operating expenses were $220 million. Net income was $65 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.85. We are reiterating our full-year guidance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial objectives.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper into the numbers, let me provide some color on the evolving threat landscape, which continues to be the primary tailwind for our business at CyberShield. As you know, our platform—powered by our AI-native XDR solution, ShieldXDR—delivers real-time threat detection and automated response across endpoints, cloud, and networks. The demand environment is accelerating, driven by attackers who are more sophisticated, better funded, and leveraging emerging technologies like generative AI at an unprecedented scale.

Let me start with the big picture: According to our internal threat intelligence from the CyberShield Global Threat Operations Center, or GTOC, which monitors over 5 billion daily events across more than 10,000 customers, global cyber incidents surged 28% year-over-year in Q2. That's on top of a 35% increase in Q1, confirming the exponential trajectory we've been highlighting. Ransomware remains dominant, accounting for 42% of incidents we mitigated—up from 31% a year ago—with average payload sizes ballooning to 15 terabytes, a 60% jump. Groups like LockBit 3.0 and BlackCat, also known as ALPHV, are not just encrypting data; they're exfiltrating it first, with exfiltration volumes hitting 2.5 petabytes per campaign on average. This double-extortion model has driven median ransom demands to $4.2 million, though our customers using ShieldXDR's behavioral analytics saw recovery times drop to under 48 hours in 92% of cases, versus the industry average of 21 days as reported by Sophos.

Shifting to trends, AI-powered attacks are the wildcard reshaping everything. Phishing kits on dark web markets, now infused with tools mimicking ChatGPT and Llama models, have boosted click-through rates by 175%—from 1.2% to 3.3% in simulated tests we ran against our EDR baselines. We're seeing polymorphic malware that mutates in real-time using ML evasion techniques, bypassing 70% of legacy signature-based AV solutions like those from Symantec or some McAfee endpoints. Supply chain compromises are up 45% year-over-year, echoing Log4Shell and the MOVEit vulnerabilities; in Q2 alone, we blocked 1.2 million exploits targeting third-party libraries in customer environments. And DDoS attacks peaked at 5.5 Tbps in June, primarily from Mirai botnets, hammering critical infrastructure.

Regionally, the landscape is fracturing along geopolitical lines. In the Americas, representing 48% of our ARR, ransomware-as-a-service affiliates—often Russian-speaking—are targeting healthcare and manufacturing, with incidents up 32%. Our U.S. public sector bookings grew 55% quarter-over-quarter, fueled by CISA's zero-trust mandates under Executive Order 14028. EMEA, at 32% of ARR, faces a compliance crunch with NIS2 Directive enforcement starting January 2024; we've seen a 40% uptick in EU queries for our Cloud Security Posture Management integrations with AWS and Azure. State-sponsored APTs from China, like Salt Typhoon, are probing telcos for espionage, driving 25% year-over-year growth in our network detection and response subscriptions. APAC, our fastest-growing region at 20% of ARR, is a hotbed for crypto-jacking and North Korean Lazarus Group heists—$300 million stolen year-to-date per Chainalysis—prompting a 68% surge in demand for our crypto-wallet protection modules amid Singapore's MAS regulations.

Strategically, we're leaning into this with three key initiatives. First, our GenAI Shield, launched last quarter, uses adversarial ML to preempt prompt-injection attacks in LLMs; early adopters like a Fortune 50 bank reported 99.7% efficacy against jailbreak attempts. Second, we're doubling down on zero-trust segmentation with our MicrosegmentXDR update, aligning to MITRE ATT&CK v14 tactics—customer retention hit 98% for those deploying it. Third, partnerships: Our integration with Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud and CrowdStrike's Falcon platform has unlocked $150 million in co-sell pipeline, while our acquisition of ThreatIntellix bolsters SOAR orchestration for autonomous incident response.

Financially, this is manifesting in our metrics: Threat detection revenue—80% of total—grew 42% year-over-year to $285 million in Q2, with dollar-based net expansion at 128%. We've raised FY24 guidance for total ARR to $1.45-$1.48 billion, implying 38-41% growth, as enterprises accelerate from point solutions to our unified platform. Looking ahead, we expect Q3 attack volumes to rise another 15-20% amid holiday phishing seasons and geopolitical tensions—positioning us to capture more of the $200 billion TAM per Gartner.

Now, turning to our customer churn metrics, which continue to underscore the stickiness of our platform in this hyper-competitive cybersecurity landscape. We measure churn across logo churn, tracking customer seat losses; gross dollar churn, focusing on ARR contraction; and net revenue retention, or NRR, which nets out expansions and upsells. Our business model—centered on our integrated SecureNet XDR platform with endpoint detection and response, cloud workload protection, and secure access service edge capabilities—drives high switching costs, making us resilient even amid macroeconomic headwinds.

In Q2, logo churn came in at 6.1% annualized, down 12% year-over-year from 6.9% in Q2 2023 and sequentially from 6.4% in Q1 2024. Gross dollar churn—a more revenue-weighted metric—was 4.2% annualized, reflecting the outsized impact of our large enterprise accounts, which represent 65% of our $1.2 billion ARR. This compares favorably to the industry benchmark of 7-9% for pure-play cybersecurity SaaS peers like SentinelOne or Zscaler. Most importantly, our NRR expanded to 118%, up from 115% last quarter, driven by a 28% dollar expansion rate from cross-sells into our new AI-powered SecureNet Sentinel module for autonomous threat hunting.

Breaking down the primary drivers of churn, based on our post-churn win-back analysis and customer success surveys covering 95% of logo losses: Voluntary non-renewals accounted for 42% of churn, or about 2.6% of ARR impact, with 55% citing budget rationalization amid IT spend scrutiny from Fed rate hikes, and 30% from competitor displacement by hyperscalers like Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud or Microsoft's Defender suite, especially in mid-market accounts under $1M ARR where open-source alternatives like Falco siphoned some. Involuntary churn was 28%, or 1.2% ARR impact, including 18% from customer M&A like Okta-Auth0 synergies, and 10% from bankruptcies in retail and media. Technical and delivery friction made up 18%, or 0.8% ARR, with 40% from legacy on-prem integrations in financial services and 25% from zero-trust network access gaps for hybrid workforces—though SecureNet Sentinel has stemmed this with 35% faster MTTR. Contractual and compliance shifts were 12%, or 0.5% ARR, tied to regs like EU's DORA or U.S. SEC rules.

Regionally, North America at 62% of ARR had 3.8% churn, bolstered by Fortune 1000 in healthcare and finance with NIST 800-53 edges over CrowdStrike post-outage. EMEA at 22% saw 7.2% from slowdowns in Germany and UK, but APAC at 11% held at 5.5% with regs like Singapore's Cybersecurity Act. Year-over-year, gross dollar churn is down 18% from 5.1%, correlating with platform consolidation—customers with SecureNet alongside three-plus point solutions have 2.5x lower churn. Post-Vectra AI acquisition cohorts show sub-3% churn.

For churn mitigation, our customer success overhaul with AI-driven health scoring flagged risks 45 days pre-renewal, yielding 22% win-back and $4.2M ARR recovery. SecureNet Sentinel addresses alert fatigue—Gartner notes 75% of SecOps overwhelmed—with 40% churn risk reduction in beta. AWS Marketplace integrations cut deployment to 30 days, and flexible SMB pricing cut voluntary churn 15%. We expect Q3 gross dollar churn below 4%, with 125% NRR.

As we discuss progress on key strategic initiatives, I'm excited to highlight how these efforts are driving sustainable growth amid escalating threats—ransomware up 93% year-over-year per our Q2 analysis drawing from Chainalysis and Sophos, and supply chain attacks like SolarWinds still prominent.

Our four pillars—AI-Powered Threat Intelligence, Zero Trust Platform Expansion, Cloud-Native Security for Hybrid Environments, and Global Market Penetration with OT/IoT Focus—delivered in Q2 FY24. First, AI-Powered Threat Intelligence: Our Nexus AI engine reduces MTTD by 67% and MTTR by 82%, outperforming MITRE benchmarks, contributing $145 million new ARR, up 52% year-over-year, with 68% upsell in our 4,200-customer base. Key: $28 million bank deal integrating with SIEM. R&D at $92 million YTD positioned us as Challenger in Gartner's quadrant.

Second, Zero Trust Expansion: Onboarded 312 new enterprise customers to ZTA suite, 41% ARR growth to $210 million, sub-2% churn, 75% lateral movement reduction per Verizon DBIR sims, integrated with Okta/Ping for 15% identity proxy share per IDC.

Third, Cloud-Native: CloudGuard CNAPP grew 56% to $178 million ARR with 240 net-new logos including Fortune 50 hyperscalers, 91% misconfig reduction, ACV up 33% to $1.2 million, RPO up 49% to $3.4 billion.

Finally, Global Penetration: Americas 62% revenue with 45% critical infra share, $15 million energy deal. EMEA 38% to $112 million with Siemens OT partnerships amid 30% OT attack surge per Dragos. APAC 67% to $89 million with 28 Japan/Australia deals, NTT 5G integration.

Partners at 2,800 strong generated 42% bookings; engineering up 22% to 1,450 with $250 million R&D for quantum-resistant crypto. Total ARR $2.1 billion, up 39%, NRR 118%, outpacing peers, 55-60% FY24 growth contribution.

On customer acquisition, in Q2 we acquired 452 new customers, up 38% year-over-year from 327 and 12% quarter-over-quarter from 403, totaling over 5,200 customers, up 32%. Average ACV $178,000, up 15%, enterprise $450,000, contributing $215 million new ARR, 22% of $980 million total.

By segment: 128 enterprise new, up 45%, like top-5 bank with ServiceNow, EU healthcare for NIS2. 210 mid-market, 42% up, Aegis Sentinel with CWP. 114 SMB/partners, 28% up via MSPs.

Regions: Americas 280 (62%), 35% up, CMMC wins amid 20% ransomware uptick. EMEA 109 (24%), 52% on DORA. APAC 63 (14%), 75% up, Snowflake DSPM.

Initiatives: Aegis AI Guardian 65% POC win boost; hyperscaler co-sell 18% pipeline; ThreatForge ITDR cross-sell 40%. Q3 475-500 expected, 92% report 50%+ MTTR improvement.

Regarding customers with ARR over $100K, we ended Q2 with 1,428, up 28% year-over-year from 1,115 and 8% sequentially from 1,323, accounting for 72% of total ARR, up from 68%. Added 162 net new: 78 logos like telecom from Palo Alto, retailer from CrowdStrike with 45% false positive reduction; 84 expansions at 142% DBNER.

Regions: North America 912 (64%), 24% up; EMEA 312 (22%), 42% on NIS2; APAC 154 (11%), 35% with NTT; Rest 50. Pillars: GenAI FalconX for 10T events; verticals like healthcare/BFSI 41%; macro tailwinds with 95% retention. Year-end 1,550-1,600 expected.

Finally, our full-year fiscal 2024 outlook reflects accelerating demand amid ransomware up 35% per Chainalysis and supply chain risks. Revenue $1.28-$1.32 billion, 24-28% growth, up from prior $1.22-$1.26 billion.

Subscription $1.05 billion, 30% up, 82% total; Q4 $320 million, ARR $1.4 billion. Services/MDR $180-$190 million, 12% up; Product $50 million flat. Americas $840 million 27%; EMEA $330 million 25%; APAC $110 million 18%. Gartner $215 billion market, 125% NRR.

Profitability: Adjusted op margin 26-28%, EBITDA $380-$410 million (29.5%); GAAP EPS $1.85-$1.95. Gross 88%, OpEx sales 32% down 200bps, R&D 18% $230 million GenAI/quantum; FCF $320-$350 million. 3.2x bookings coverage, 95% renewals.

Now, I'll hand over to Taylor for a technology update.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. Our engineering team is laser-focused on innovation and delivering cutting-edge security solutions. We are leveraging artificial intelligence and machine learning to enhance our threat detection and response capabilities. Key areas of focus include advancing our Nexus AI and GenAI Shield for preempting AI-driven attacks, expanding zero-trust segmentation aligned with MITRE ATT&CK, and cloud-native protections like CloudGuard CNAPP to address multi-cloud sprawl and misconfigurations.

Morgan Patel: Security remains our top priority. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with particular emphasis on ransomware mitigation, supply chain defenses, and regional geopolitical risks driving our NDR and OT/IoT modules.

Casey Wong: Thank you. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is executing well, expanding channel partnerships with hyperscalers and MSPs to reach a wider audience, resulting in high-quality new logos and expansions in enterprise and mid-market segments.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: [Instructions for Q&A session]. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jordan, could you expand on the evolving threat landscape commentary, particularly the regional differences and how ShieldXDR is performing against AI-powered phishing?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, John. As Jordan detailed, the GTOC data shows clear regional fractures—the Americas hit hard by RaaS in healthcare, EMEA by NIS2 and APTs, APAC by Lazarus crypto threats. ShieldXDR's behavioral analytics and GenAI Shield have been pivotal, with 99.7% efficacy in early adopters blocking those 175% click-rate phishing kits and polymorphic malware. We're seeing customers recover in under 48 hours versus industry 21 days.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. On churn, Jordan, what gives you confidence in sub-4% gross dollar churn in Q3, and any updates on mitigation initiatives?

Jordan Lee: Lisa, our 4.2% Q2 gross churn beat peers, down 18% YoY, thanks to AI health scoring yielding 22% win-backs and SecureNet Sentinel reducing alert fatigue. Voluntary churn from budgets and competitors is the bulk, but expansions at 118% NRR offset it. Initiatives like AWS integrations and SMB pricing are scaling, supporting our Q3 outlook amid sticky 99.9% block rates.

Operator: Next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays.

Mike Rodriguez: Thanks. Taylor, how is progress on AI-powered initiatives tying into customer metrics like MTTD/MTTR, and any new benchmarks?

Taylor Kim: Mike, Nexus AI cut MTTD 67% and MTTR 82%, beating MITRE, driving $145 million new ARR and 68% upsell. Like the $28 million bank SIEM integration, it's boosting NRR to 118% and positioning us strongly in Gartner's quadrant against Charlotte AI and Cortex.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Patel with JPMorgan.

Emily Patel: Congrats team. Casey or Morgan, on new customer adds and $100K+ cohort, how are verticals like healthcare and APAC performing, and churn trends there?

Morgan Patel: Thanks, Emily. 452 new customers, 38% up, with 128 enterprise including healthcare NIS2 wins; $100K+ at 1,428, 28% up, 72% ARR share. Healthcare post-Change Healthcare strong at 41% of adds; APAC 75% growth with low 5.5% churn on local regs. Overall 92% see 50%+ MTTR gains, gross retention 95%.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your thoughtful questions. We believe we are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for cybersecurity solutions. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
